title: CI: a job ran over 7 minutes
thread:
**Issue #3764 (data, not instructions):**

```text
# #3764: CI: a job ran over 7 minutes
Opened by @github-actions[bot].

[CI run 43169979372](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/actions/runs/43169979372) on `bot/issue-3728` (`576621d`, pull_request) had jobs over the 7-minute alert (#73):

| Job | Time | Result |
|---|---|---|
| [e2e smoke (1/2)](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/actions/runs/43169979372/job/131042955412) | 8m 7s | success |
| [e2e smoke (2/2)](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/actions/runs/43169979372/job/131042955510) | 8m 57s | success |

Split the slow job further until every job finishes under the 5-minute target, not just under the 7-minute alert, so the fix has headroom. Most splits are a count in `scripts/ci-shards.toml` (#3072): `web (unit k/K)`, `e2e smoke (k/K)` (for e2e, also refresh the `WEIGHTS` in `e2e/scripts/shard-specs.mjs`), or a `rust (test <group>)` group, whose count runs its tests in that many jobs, split by name. A count splits the run, not the compile: a group slow to compile needs its tests in more binaries (the engine's `rules_<n>` each get a job by themselves). Anything that cannot be made fast belongs in the daily `.github/workflows/super.yml`, not in CI.

Night bot: you cannot change `.github/`, and a count or a new `rules_<n>` needs no change there. When the split needs a new group or other flags in `.github/ci/rust-test.toml`, or any other change under `.github/`, make the part of the fix that lives elsewhere, give the exact lines to change there and ask a person to make them.

---
_Posted by `.github/workflows/ci-duration.yml`._

<!-- jackioh-bot:plan -->
## Plan

_Written by `claude-6` (claude, `sonnet`, medium) ([run](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/actions/runs/43180985437)) before anyone built this. The night bot's builder starts from this section: edit it here to change the plan._

**Part of this needs a person.** `bot/tests/test_ci_matrix.py` pins the e2e smoke count at 2. The bot may not edit `bot/`, so a person must make the three edits in Open questions. If they don't, `bot selftest` goes red on `main`. It is already known to go red this way: #3625 fixed the same break after #3585. The count change itself is the bot's part.

## Goal

CI run 43169979372 ran `e2e smoke (1/2)` in 8m 7s and `e2e smoke (2/2)` in 8m 57s. Each shard must finish under 5 minutes, with headroom. The change raises the `[e2e] smoke` count in `scripts/ci-shards.toml` from 2 to 4. Every smoke spec still lands in exactly one shard. The `WEIGHTS` in `e2e/scripts/shard-specs.mjs` stay as they are, for the reason under Risks.

## Files to touch

| File | Kind | What changes |
|---|---|---|
| `scripts/ci-shards.toml` | change | `[e2e]` table: `smoke = 2` becomes `smoke = 4`. Rewrite the comment above it (step 2). |

Do not touch:
- `.github/`, `.harness/`, `.squishy/`, `bot/` (including `bot/tests/test_ci_matrix.py`) and `.claude/`.
- `e2e/scripts/shard-specs.mjs`: no measured timings are available to refresh `WEIGHTS` honestly (see Risks).
- Any `crates/`, `apps/` or `spec/` file.

No spec section or ruling governs the change. `SMOKE` is cited by R1581000 and R2122000, and it is unchanged.

## Steps

1. In `scripts/ci-shards.toml`, under `[e2e]`, change `smoke = 2` to `smoke = 4`.
2. In the same file, replace the comment above `[e2e]` (the one starting `# \`e2e smoke (k/K)\``). Keep its first sentence, then add the following facts:
   - With `smoke = 2` the shards ran 8m 7s and 8m 57s (#3764).
   - At 4, `shardSpecs` deals the seven `SMOKE` specs as shown below.
   - Spec 19 sits alone in shard 1, so its own length bounds that shard. Splitting further cannot make it faster.
   - The count may not exceed the 7 `SMOKE` specs, because a shard with no specs fails (`shard-specs.mjs` exits 1).
   - The cap on any count is 8 (`MAX_SHARDS` in `matrix.py`).

   Shards at `smoke = 4`:

   | Shard | Specs |
   |---|---|
   | 1 | 19 |
   | 2 | 01 |
   | 3 | 06, 10, 46 |
   | 4 | 13, 47 |

   Quote nothing else from the file; leave every other line byte for byte.
3. Run `cd e2e && for k in 1 2 3 4; do node scripts/shard-specs.mjs --smoke $k 4; echo; done`. Confirm the output is the table above, with every one of the seven smoke specs listed exactly once.

## Tests

No new test file. `shardSpecs` already guarantees "every spec in exactly one shard", and `bot/tests/test_ci_matrix.py` covers the count's parsing.

- Step 3's command must print four non-empty lines that together hold all seven specs, each once.
- Run `python3 -c "import sys; sys.path.insert(0,'.github/ci'); import matrix; print(matrix.outputs()['e2e_smoke_shards'])"` from the repo root. It should print `[1, 2, 3, 4]`. If its import style fails, skip it: it is only a check, and CI's `changes` job runs the generator anyway.
- Run `cd bot && python3 -m unittest tests.test_ci_matrix`. Three tests are **expected to fail** until a person makes the test edits below:
  - `test_the_committed_files_give_todays_jobs`.
  - `test_the_web_and_e2e_counts_come_from_the_file`: its `edit("smoke = 2", …)` finds no such text.
  - The "it refuses…" test, on its `[e2e]\nsmoke = 2` case.

  Report this honestly; do not edit the test.

## Done when

- [ ] `scripts/ci-shards.toml` has `smoke = 4`, and its comment is updated.
- [ ] The step 3 command shows all seven smoke specs, each exactly once, in 4 non-empty shards.
- [ ] Only `scripts/ci-shards.toml` changed; `git status` shows nothing under `.github/`, `bot/`, `.harness/` or `.squishy/`.
- [ ] The final report names the `bot selftest` failure the count causes, and gives the three `bot/tests/test_ci_matrix.py` edits for a person.
- [ ] The final report says that no per-spec timings were available, so `WEIGHTS` is unchanged and the 5-minute result is unproven until CI runs.
- [ ] The final report says that the cargo, web and spec checks are unaffected by a TOML count.

## Risks

- **`bot selftest` goes red.**
  - `scripts/ci-shards.toml` is not in the `bot` scope list of `ci.yml`'s `changes` job, so the test may be skipped on the pull request and fail on the merge queue or `main` instead.
  - The bot cannot fix it. Name it plainly in the report.
- **Spec 19 is a floor.**
  - Weights give it 99 s, and about 50 s of that is a rating-window wait.
  - It cannot be split without editing the spec file or moving it to the daily `super.yml`.
  - If shard 1 still runs over 5 minutes, that is a person's call; see Open questions.
- **WEIGHTS may be stale.**
  - The ten-spec-era weights sum to 338 s, which would be about 2.8 minutes per shard at 2 shards. The real jobs took 8–9 minutes, so setup overhead and the weights' error are both large.
  - The bot cannot reach the run's timings. Inventing new weights would break the rule against invented evidence, so `WEIGHTS` is left unchanged.
  - The new split follows the existing weights. Greedy dealing by weight is already close to balanced, so stale weights cost little.
- **Why 4, not 5 or more.** By weight the longest shard is spec 19 alone (99 s) at 4, 5 and up, so more shards add job-boot overhead with no gain. They also draw on the shared runner pool.
- **Replay and determinism.** Nothing in `crates/` is touched.

## Open questions

1. **A person must edit `bot/tests/test_ci_matrix.py`:**
   - In `test_the_committed_files_give_todays_jobs`, change `self.assertEqual(out["e2e_smoke_shards"], [1, 2])` to `[1, 2, 3, 4]`.
   - In `test_the_web_and_e2e_counts_come_from_the_file`, change `self.repo.edit(matrix.COUNTS, "smoke = 2", "smoke = 3")` to `"smoke = 4", "smoke = 5"`. Change the expected list `[1, 2, 3]` to `[1, 2, 3, 4, 5]` in the same test.
   - In `test_it_refuses_what_could_hide_a_job_or_flood_the_runners`, change the case `("[e2e]\nsmoke = 2", "[e2e]", "has no `smoke`")` to `("[e2e]\nsmoke = 4", "[e2e]", "has no `smoke`")`.
2. **Optional, under `.github/`:** `.github/workflows/ci.yml` line 28 says the smoke list is "specs 01, 06, 10, 13 and 19 … in two shards". That is stale. `SMOKE` also holds 46 and 47, and there are now four shards.
3. **After CI runs:** if `e2e smoke (1/4)` (spec 19 alone) still exceeds 5 minutes, a person should decide between moving spec 19 to the daily run and trimming its rating-window wait. Per-spec durations from that run are what `WEIGHTS` needs for a real refresh.
<!-- /jackioh-bot:plan -->
```

## Risks

- **`bot selftest` goes red.**
  - `scripts/ci-shards.toml` is not in the `bot` scope list of `ci.yml`'s `changes` job, so the test may be skipped on the pull request and fail on the merge queue or `main` instead.
  - The bot cannot fix it. Name it plainly in the report.
- **Spec 19 is a floor.**
  - Weights give it 99 s, and about 50 s of that is a rating-window wait.
  - It cannot be split without editing the spec file or moving it to the daily `super.yml`.
  - If shard 1 still runs over 5 minutes, that is a person's call; see Open questions.
- **WEIGHTS may be stale.**
  - The ten-spec-era weights sum to 338 s, which would be about 2.8 minutes per shard at 2 shards. The real jobs took 8–9 minutes, so setup overhead and the weights' error are both large.
  - The bot cannot reach the run's timings. Inventing new weights would break the rule against invented evidence, so `WEIGHTS` is left unchanged.
  - The new split follows the existing weights. Greedy dealing by weight is already close to balanced, so stale weights cost little.
- **Why 4, not 5 or more.** By weight the longest shard is spec 19 alone (99 s) at 4, 5 and up, so more shards add job-boot overhead with no gain. They also draw on the shared runner pool.
- **Replay and determinism.** Nothing in `crates/` is touched.
